svg.text: Straight up, the F2 layer returns only frequencies below its critical frequency foF2; slanted, it returns foF2 × sec i, so the MUF climbs with distance until the ray grazes the horizon
(each line ends at its station's longest single hop). A band whose dashed line lies above foF2 is not heard near the transmitter but is heard far away: the skip zone. Daylight
stations (orange) sit far above night ones (blue): sunlight ionises the F2 layer.
